proof:
The sum of the simplex vertices is zero, so $H_0>0$ and $\sum_{i=1}^d\Delta_i=(d+1)H_0$. The prescribed vertex values for $u_{\rm can}$ sum to zero, so their affine interpolation is linear. On a proper trace satisfying the hypothesis, the edge intercept ratios from $r_zv_0$ are $t_z/(r_z\Delta_i)\in(0,1]$. The trace simplex has volume $Vt_z^d/\prod_i\Delta_i$ by multiplying these ratios and the original fiber volume. The new apex margin is $(d/H_0)t_z$. Its gap from each other vertex is $(d+1)r_z$. It therefore captures $V\min\{r_z^d,[((d/H_0)t_z)_+/(d+1)]^d\}$ by homothety from the apex until saturation. This is no larger than the original trace by AM–GM on the $\Delta_i$. A zero-volume original trace has $t_z\le0$ and the new trace is also null. A full original trace cannot gain volume. The trace at $z_0$ is proper because its centroid is interior and $u\ne0$. There the AM–GM inequality is strict unless all $\Delta_i$ coincide, which is exactly the positive-canonical case. For an affine centroid graph $c_z=Az+b$, subtract $c_z$ in the continuous coordinate. This shear preserves bases, volumes and closed halfspaces, and sends the given centroid to $(z_0,0)$.

The same homothety formula with apex margin $dr_z+\beta\cdot(z-z_0)$ proves $Q_+$. Reversing the full normal complements the cap up to the nonvertical volume-null boundaries, proving the opposite formula. For a pure-base cap, multiply its tilt by a sufficiently large positive finite factor and use a fixed canonical normal. Strictly positive base margins then give full traces and strictly negative margins give zero traces, since there are finitely many fibers. The base boundary fibers can only lose volume. The two clipping thresholds in $Q_+$ give continuity and the stated polynomial pieces.

For compact representatives restrict tilts to $L=\operatorname{span}(P-z_0)$ without changing their offsets. If $L=0$, use the singleton tilt zero. Otherwise choose orthonormal coordinates on $L$, write $v_z$ for the coordinate row of $z-z_0$, and classify the given offsets as interior, at or above the upper saturation threshold, or at or below the lower threshold. Keep the interior offsets as equalities and impose the corresponding weak inequalities for the saturated ones. This feasible system has no line because a line direction would annihilate every row $v_z$. From any feasible point whose equality and tight rows do not span, move along a nonzero direction perpendicular to them. Short steps in either sign are feasible; in at least one sign a new row becomes tight at finite distance, since there is no line. Its pairing with the direction is nonzero, so the rank increases. Repeating yields a feasible point determined by a square independent set of rows, whose right-hand sides have absolute value at most $d\max_z r_z$. The finitely many inverse row matrices thus give one uniform bound in these coordinates. Its closed coordinate box is compact. The new tilt preserves every fiber mass by the clipping rule, so continuous $Q_+$ attains both extrema there.
statement:
Let $T$ be a centered $d$-simplex, $d\ge2$, of volume $V$ with vertices $v_0,\ldots,v_d$, and let a finite nonempty $P\subset\mathbb Z^n$ carry fibers $r_zT$, $r_z>0$. Fix $z_0\in P$. For a cap $u\cdot x+\alpha\cdot(z-z_0)\ge0$ with $u\ne0$, suppose $H_0=u\cdot v_0>u\cdot v_i$ for each $i>0$. Put $\Delta_i=H_0-u\cdot v_i$ and $t_z=H_0r_z+\alpha\cdot(z-z_0)$. Suppose every trace is volume-full, volume-zero, or satisfies $0<t_z\le r_z\min_{i>0}\Delta_i$. Define $u_{\rm can}$ by its values $d$ at $v_0$ and $-1$ at all other vertices. Replacing the cap by
$$u_{\rm can}\cdot x+(d/H_0)\alpha\cdot(z-z_0)\ge0$$
does not increase the volume on any fiber, and strictly decreases the summed volume unless $u$ is a positive multiple of $u_{\rm can}$. The assertion also holds for fibers with an affine centroid graph after the volume-preserving centering shear.

For any canonical vertex direction, the whole closed-cap volume function of the tilt is the same:
$$
 Q_+(\beta)=V\sum_{z\in P}\min\left\{r_z^d,\left[\frac{(d r_z+\beta\cdot(z-z_0))_+}{d+1}\right]^d\right\}.
$$
The opposite direction gives $M-Q_+(-\beta)$, where $M=V\sum_zr_z^d$. The function $Q_+$ is continuous and piecewise polynomial of degree at most $d$, with breaks at $\beta\cdot(z-z_0)=-dr_z$ and $r_z$. The vectors of canonical fiber masses have representatives in a fixed compact set of tilts. Consequently the minimum over canonical and opposite-canonical caps through the mark is $\min\{\min_\beta Q_+(\beta),\,M-\max_\beta Q_+(\beta)\}$, with both extrema attained. A pure-base cap through the mark can be replaced by a canonical cap of no greater volume.
title: Canonical cap replacement for centered simplex fibers with only vertex-cap proper traces
